rationale: M60.R8 (#934) — the framework ORDER contract, which php never had. The lane published `[...detectedFrameworks]`, a Set's INSERTION order, so `metadata.framework` — the primary pick — was decided by whichever marker happened to fire first in the FILE. That is python's defect verbatim: R8's register records python's second caught mutant as 'the emitted order following import order instead of the marker table', swift and objective-c carry SWIFT_FRAMEWORK_ORDER / OBJC_FRAMEWORK_ORDER, and csharp's CS_FRAMEWORK_ORDER is the rule python's own header cites. php's row never named it because that row already carried a different debt (the two dead markers, #931) and a lane's row can only hold what someone measured. This file `use`s Symfony BEFORE Illuminate on purpose, so document order is the INVERSE of the table order: the pre-fix reading was ["Symfony","Laravel"] with Symfony primary, and the pinned reading is ["Laravel","Symfony"] with Laravel primary. The sibling php/framework-surface-pins could not hold this rule — its namespace fires Laravel first, so both orders agree there. The array is pinned exactly (not as a must-include list) because ORDER is the whole contract; forbidFrameworks is the negative half.

expectMetadata.comment: TABLE order, not document order — Symfony's marker fires first in this file (`use Symfony\...` @ line 21) and Laravel's second (`use Illuminate\...` @ line 22), and the published list is the inverse of that. This is the pin the mutant php/framework-order-document reverses.

expectRelationships.comment: the base clause is still published as written; ordering the framework list must not disturb the heritage edge
